title: JSON-to-CSV conversion renders nested address as [object Object]
reason: Checkpoint assertion failed: "the CSV output contains the word Paris"

verdict.title: JSON-to-CSV conversion renders nested address as [object Object]
verdict.oneLiner: The CSV output shows "[object Object]" instead of the nested address value, so it omits Paris.
verdict.rootCause: The converter puts the whole address object into one CSV cell instead of extracting its city value.
verdict.suggestion: Update the CSV conversion to flatten nested fields such as address.city, or serialize nested objects in a readable form instead of showing "[object Object]".

attempts.agentSummary:
I fixed BUG-003's sibling, BUG-001: `serializeValue` in `src/tools/json-to-csv/json-to-csv.service.ts:20` turned every cell into text with `String(value)`, so a nested object like `address` became `[object Object]`. Objects and arrays are now converted with `JSON.stringify`, and everything else still uses `String`. The flow's row should now read `Alice,alice@example.test,{\"city\":\"Paris\"}`, so Paris is in the output; the quotes inside the cell are escaped the same way the tool already escapes quotes.

I also added a unit test for nested objects in `json-to-csv.service.test.ts`. I haven't seen any test pass: the vitest run needed approval and was blocked, and per the rules for this session I didn't start the app or run Gremlin. Kane's re-run of the flow will be the real check.

One related flow, BUG-003 (a single JSON object instead of an array gives an empty output with no error), is a separate bug and I didn't change it.
